A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2ec/RecPO research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including content moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, ablations and optimization analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3, plus appendix latency measurements and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, architecture and embedding analyses, reasoning annotations, larger-model experiments and additional-domain results.

M1.justification: The dual-head architecture, trajectory sampling, fused reward, clipped joint objective and highest-advantage trajectory selection remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. The new gradient appendix explains the existing method; classifier-head and pooling alternatives are experimental controls.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates CDs and Vinyl, Video Games and Musical Instruments. v2 retains these datasets and adds Electronics, GoodReads and MovieLens in Appendix I and Figure 6, substantially extending evaluation coverage to additional product, book and movie domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SDPO*, LLaRA* and SPRec in the Gemma comparison block. The latency comparison adds SASRec, D3 and LLaRA to LangPTune. Figure 6 introduces further comparators, including RW, DMPO, RosePO, TALLRec, MoRec and ChatRec; GoodReads and MovieLens baseline values are explicitly borrowed from cited papers.

E3.justification: The original dataset splits, preprocessing and ranking metrics remain unchanged. New protocols include full-catalog adaptations of SDPO/LLaRA, Gemma-9B evaluation, annotation of 100 reasoning outputs per test set using humans and GPT-4.1, and MovieLens H@1 evaluation. The latency study replaces batch sizes 1, 4 and 8 with batch size 1 and adds a vLLM condition.

E4.justification: v2 adds a classifier-head ablation, comparisons of last-state, pooling and special-token embeddings, reasoning-versus-no-reasoning scaling tests, and systematic analysis of seven reasoning behaviors. Existing advantage-estimator, sampling, group-size and four case studies are retained. The efficiency analysis gains method comparisons but loses its batch-size sweep.

E5.justification: v1's latency table reports means and standard deviations. v2 newly specifies three independent runs of 100 queries but reports only means. This establishes changed reporting, without establishing an increase in repetitions. Table 1 retains its p-value-below-0.05 significance convention.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, ablation, reasoning-behavior, scaling and additional-domain results. Original R2ec scores in Table 1 are unchanged, while Gemma D3's Video Games H@20 changes from 0.0378 to 0.0478 and improvement percentages are revised. New Table 6 reports Gemma-9B N@5 of 0.0451 versus 0.0370 without reasoning, but H@10 of 0.0878 versus 0.0893. Latency results are replaced under a revised protocol, preventing a direct cross-version speedup comparison.

T1.justification: New Appendix F derives how recommendation gradients propagate through the reasoning hidden state and live item encoder. This adds a local mathematical derivation absent from v1; the original equations, objective and formal setup remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 retains the unified-model and annotation-free optimization claims but makes lower latency against conventional and reasoning-augmented LLM recommenders, context-aware interpretability and broader adaptability prominent contributions. The abstract and contribution list remove v1's headline percentage improvements and its emphasis on increasing reasoning length.

C2.justification: v2 extends v1's anecdotal domain/backbone interpretation into a seven-strategy account of context-dependent reasoning. It also explains special-token underperformance through limited LoRA training and interprets new scaling and efficiency findings. The original limitations concerning decoding cost and parameter-efficient rather than full-model tuning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The availability statement expands from code to code and checkpoints. v2 also documents candidate-prompt removal and constrained generation for the new baseline adaptations, plus the new annotation and inference configurations. Existing hardware, software versions, LoRA settings, core hyperparameters, prompts and training pipeline are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including SPRec, Phased Training for LLM-Powered Text Retrieval Models and Order-Agnostic Identifier, alongside limited background expansion. The central positioning around unified reasoning and recommendation remains. LLaRA and SDPO were already cited in v1; their new experimental participation is a baseline change.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, contribution list and conclusion are rewritten around efficiency and reasoning behavior. Related Work moves from the main text to Appendix A, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into optimization, reasoning-behavior and efficiency sections, with new analytical appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds the reasoning-behavior heatmap, embedding and scaling tables, and three additional-domain comparison panels. It expands Tables 1–2 and replaces the appendix batch-size latency table with a main-text method comparison. The NeurIPS format substantially changes widths, sizing and placement; existing architecture, optimization and case-study figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added comparators and targeted classifier-head, embedding and scaling controls strengthen support for the unchanged method, while additional domains broaden its empirical validation. However, revised Table 1 improvement percentages do not consistently match the displayed scores, the latency study drops standard deviations, and new-domain protocols have limited local detail. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall gain despite the substantially broader evidence.
